core_obligations: Forward direction: for a morphism U -> V use that coverings in the chaotic topology are isomorphisms to obtain from quasi-coherence a two-term presentation of F restricted to C/V, and use exactness of taking sections to get presentations of F(V) and of F(U) as modules (proof lines 3554-3568).
Conclude from these two presentations that the canonical map F(V) tensor_{O(V)} O(U) -> F(U) is an isomorphism (proof lines 3569-3576).
Converse: assume the base-change condition for all U -> V and reconstruct presentations exhibiting F as quasi-coherent, completing the proof up to line 3593.
proof_roadmap: Exploit that coverings in the chaotic topology are isomorphisms.
Turn quasi-coherence into module presentations and compare along U -> V.
For the converse, build the presentations from the base-change condition.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes quasi-coherence of a module on a category endowed with the chaotic topology by the condition that for every morphism U -> V the canonical base-change map F(V) tensor_{O(V)} O(U) -> F(U) is an isomorphism. The forward direction uses that in the chaotic topology every covering is an isomorphism, so quasi-coherence provides a presentation of the restriction of F to C/V whose sections compute F(V) because taking sections is exact; the same computation over U, together with the presentation, shows the displayed map is an isomorphism (proof lines 3554-3576). The converse reconstructs the required presentations from the module-theoretic base-change condition, completing the proof up to line 3593. H2: the translation between sheaf-theoretic quasi-coherence and the module-theoretic base-change condition is the substance.
